instruction: Configure VLC to allow play/pause control via a global hotkey, enabling usage even if VLC isn't focused.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires configuring a global hotkey for play/pause in VLC (global-key-play-pause should have a value set). Evaluator uses existing check_global_key_play_pause metric and get_vlc_config getter to read VLC configuration file and verify that global-key-play-pause is configured (has a non-empty value). Default is empty (no global hotkey), so the agent must navigate to Tools > Preferences > Hotkeys and set a global hotkey for play/pause. This is similar in complexity to the original task (changing a single VLC configuration setting).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to configure a global hotkey for play/pause in VLC
Getter (get_vlc_config) correctly extracts the VLC configuration file from the appropriate OS-specific location
Metric (check_global_key_play_pause) correctly checks the 'global-key-play-pause' config setting, which specifically controls global hotkeys (vs 'key-play-pause' for local hotkeys)
Logic correctly distinguishes between 'not configured' (empty value) and 'configured' (any non-empty value), which semantically matches the task requirement
Expected value '1' correctly represents 'hotkey is configured' - the metric returns '1' when the config value is non-empty
Postconfig appropriately kills and relaunches VLC to ensure configuration changes are persisted to disk and readable
Complete coverage: the single requirement (configure global hotkey) is fully verified by the evaluator
Data flow is correct: config file path -> read file -> parse for setting -> binary check (configured vs not configured) -> return score
